guidance: Move/rotate/flip parts ONLY via place_edit.py --ops (absolute ops, atomic, verified).

Moving a placed-and-routed part strands its copper: after any move on a routed board, the affected nets must be re-routed (route_edit removals + route_auto/route_critical) before the routed gates re-pass. Flag this in your summary.

violations.msg: The outline's AREA was earned but its ASPECT RATIO was not, on a canonical binding where geometry is supposed to be an output. 50.000 x 26.420 mm came out of board_edit --outline fit over a thermally-driven placement (thermal_area.json shows the work), but the 50 mm width is forced by constraints.json placement.edges pinning J1 to the left edge and J2 to the right: two 10.16 mm-deep terminals on opposite ends plus U1+C1+C2 between them cannot fit in less, and the height then follows. Heat spreads radially, so shape matters as much as area: at the same 1321 mm2, a squarer outline with the tab near the centre would put roughly 1300 mm2 within 25 mm of the tab instead of the delivered 1086.18 mm2 - about +200 mm2 of effective copper, ~1.4 C/W on the AMS table's own slope, i.e. ~10 % of the 10-15 C junction margin. RECOMMEND WAIVING for this build: the gain is small and the fix is a re-placement plus re-route plus re-pour, and the delivered layout already beat the alternatives (cand1 carried only 517 mm2 within 25 mm). Logged because it is the same species as the bb-buck defect - a geometry input that bound the design without being earned - and nothing else in the pipeline will ever notice it.

scope: fix ONLY these violations; do not touch unrelated nets/regions; re-run the failed gate when done
